articleBody:
- [ ] Check subfloor around toilet flange for softness — Soft or discolored wood indicates chronic wax ring leaks that compromise structural framing.
- [ ] Measure floor levelness across doorways and tub skirts — Uneven dips greater than standard manufacturer tolerances will crack rigid porcelain or create hollow spots.
- [ ] Take moisture meter readings across exposed plywood — Installing underlayment over wet wood traps moisture, inviting wood rot and adhesive failure.
- [ ] Inspect joists from beneath if accessible in basements or crawlspaces — Structural deflection causes tile grout lines to crack under daily foot traffic.
- [ ] Verify clearance under bathroom doors and vanity bases — Adding backer board and thick stone tile can prevent doors from swinging freely.
- [ ] Confirm waterproof membrane or underlayment compatibility — Adhesives must match the specific subfloor type and selected flooring material.
- [ ] Check plumbing flange height relative to finished floor height — A flange sitting too low below thick tile prevents a watertight wax ring seal.
- [ ] Plan perimeter expansion gaps along walls and tub aprons — Floors expand with humidity swings, requiring flexible sealant rather than rigid grout at edges.

How to use this checklist
Go through these checkpoints before purchasing flooring or signing an installation agreement. Uncovering subfloor rot or leveling problems during demolition changes project scope immediately.
